samples.question: The top panel of this image shows four upright bars - one red, one blue, one green and one orange - standing on a common black baseline. The bottom panel shows a gray wheel cut into four sectors by dark spokes running from the center to the rim. The four sectors stand for the four bars: each bar matches exactly one sector, and each bar's share of the total height of all four bars equals its sector's share of the full turn of the wheel. No length unit is drawn, so only these shares can be compared, and the left-to-right order of the bars has nothing to do with where its sector sits on the wheel. Just outside each sector, at the middle of that sector, sits a black glyph tag - a square, a circle, a triangle, or a diamond - and each glyph tags the sector it sits beside. Which glyph tags the sector that matches the red bar? Answer square, circle, triangle, or diamond.
